newsitem.title: JAPAN: Crudes ease in Asia, wet Mideast trade marks time.
newsitem.headline: Crudes ease in Asia, wet Mideast trade marks time.

text.p: Crude oil prices slipped in Asia on Wednesday as market sentiment soured following the overnight release of bearish API data, traders said.
In late Tokyo trade, January cash Brent was notionally assessed at $23.55/23.65, down from late Tuesday U.S. levels of $23.80/23.90.
The fall was triggered by weekly API data showing a rise of 1.85 million barrels in U.S. distillate stocks and an increase of 1.93 million barrels in gasoline stocks, brokers said.
In paper spreads, January and February Brent/Dubai were both assessed at around $1.75/1.80.
February/March Dubai was notionally assessed at 55/62 cents. The Dubai paper market was thin as talks over wet February Middle Eastern cargoes have yet to get into full swing, traders said.
A Japanese refiner has already bought two cargoes of February Qatar Land at QGPC plus 55 to 58 cents and one Qatar Marine at plus 45 cents, traders said.

The refiner bought the Qatari grades believing prices of light grades would firm later in the month, traders said. Sellers of February Oman are making soundings about a premium of 20 cents, but buyers have yet to emerge, traders said.

January Oman sales ended at about MPM plus 13 cents. Some traders doubted Oman would be able to fetch a premium of 20 cents, as the Oman/Dubai differential has widened to 86 cents from last month's 74 cents. An overhang of January Yemen Masila cargoes was also seen adding pressure.
At least one company appears to have agreed to buy Masila crude oil for January-March 1997 from Yemen at dated Brent minus 97 cents, traders said.
In regional grades, offers of Tapis edged up to APPI Tapis plus $1.10 after a sale to a Singapore refiner on Monday at plus $1.00, traders said. --J.Oshima/Tokyo (+81-3-5473-3706)
